This lane's dispatch instruction says to open the PR as a DRAFT with landing held, and separately says the manager merges, not the lane. Nothing here self-lands.

One substantive reason a human reads it rather than letting it through on its tier: THE DIFF CHANGES WHAT A REAL-MONEY LEG'S EVIDENCE RECORD SAYS. comms/strategy_evidence/fvg_range_15m.json is an input to scripts/ci/check_roster_promotion_evidence.py, which grades the bybit_2 roster, and this PR moves that leg from 'nothing ever measured it' to a measured net_r_oos of -10.2594. Nothing in the diff acts on that number -- no roster is edited -- but the number is now available to a lane that will.
why:
CHECKLIST ROW E25 -- 'we need to resolve the harness issue for fvg range 15' (operator, 2026-09-22).

THE CAUSE, in the code's own words. scripts/ops/build_strategy_evidence.py wrote coverage_state: 'no_harness' for fvg_range_15m with the text 'regime_debt_matrix.classify() routes nothing for this leg... A harness may still EXIST for the family -- backtest_ict_scalp.py and backtest_fvg_range.py both do -- so this is a missing classifier branch plus a lever map, not absent infrastructure.' That was correct. scripts/backtest_fvg_range.py exists, E3 wired its cost model, and nothing routed to it.

WHAT LANDS. (a) A fourth classify() branch keyed on range_lookback+third_frac, checked LAST so no already-measured leg is silently re-routed -- the same precedence convention the squeeze branch documents. MEASURED over all 55 legs in config/strategies.yaml: each of those two keys is carried by exactly one leg, so the conjunction cannot capture a leg an earlier branch should have taken. (b) _FVG_PLAIN / _FVG_LEVER_FLAG, read off backtest_fvg_range.py's own add_argument list rather than its docstring, with adx_min and tp_r deliberately in NEITHER set (no --adx-min exists; --tp-r binds only under --exit-style tp1r) so a leg declaring either degrades to `approximate` and names it instead of being certified faithful against a filter the harness never applies. (c) A build_harness_cmd branch that does NOT reuse the shared `common` list, which hard-codes --atr-stop-mult/--trail-mult that this harness does not accept -- passing them aborts the subprocess, and run_one reports a non-zero exit as 'harness failed', so a missing FLAG would have read as a broken harness. (d) tests/test_regime_debt_matrix_fvg_range.py, a sibling of the squeeze wiring test, including its strongest check: every flag the matrix passes is parsed out of the harness's real source and asserted to be declared.

EN ROUTE, A SECOND DEFECT THAT ONLY THIS CHANGE MAKES REACHABLE. _TF_TO_BYBIT_INT and _TF_TO_YF_INT both .get(timeframe, <daily>), so a timeframe MISSING from the map did not fail -- it silently fetched DAILY bars and handed them to a harness told to --resample 15m. Neither map had a 15m or 5m entry. Nothing hit it while classify() only routed 1h/2h/4h/1d legs; routing a 15m family makes it reachable, so the intraday codes are filled in (Bybit codes verified against scripts/ops/fetch_backtest_candles.py --interval's own accepted set). The Yahoo intraday entries turn a silent daily-bar substitution into a NAMED empty-feed failure past yfinance's ~60d intraday window, which is the honest outcome.

THE MEASUREMENT, AND IT IS A FAIL. comms/strategy_evidence/fvg_range_15m.json: coverage_state MEASURED, fidelity faithful, omitted_levers []. net_r_oos -10.2594 over n=17 trades, expectancy -0.6035R, 0 of 4 time-folds positive, net of the full cost stack (fee 7.5 / slippage 5.0 / funding 1.0 bps roundtrip), over 34,944 real BTCUSDT 15m bars from data.binance.vision spanning 2025-09-22 -> 2026-09-20. decision_rule RULE-D1-STAGE0-NET-OF-FULL-COST, registered 2026-09-22T05:34:08Z which is BEFORE this run, verdict fail. NOTHING WAS TUNED TO REACH THAT. The row's instruction was explicit that a measured fail is the complete outcome, and it is: against B1's four-clause bar the leg went from failing ALL FOUR clauses to failing exactly one (C4, the rule), because C1-C3 had no answer at all before.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. config/accounts.yaml and config/strategies.yaml are untouched -- rosters are Tier-3 and lane R2 is editing them concurrently. execution_costs.py is untouched (E3's fence). The four coverage_state values stay four distinct states; this PR moves one leg between two of them and adds a test asserting the no_harness state is still REACHABLE, so the fix cannot quietly retire a state by making nothing produce it.

POPULATION, because the row asked and the answer changes the row's size. MEASURED 2026-09-22 over all 52 enabled legs by importing regime_debt_matrix and calling classify(): 42 routed before, 43 after; unrouted 10 -> 9. It was never one leg. The remaining 9 are turtle_soup plus the EIGHT-leg ict_scalp_* family -- and all eight of those carry execution: live, where fvg_range_15m is only shadow. backtest_ict_scalp.py exists and nothing routes to it: the identical defect at eight times the size, on live legs. Not ported here because that harness loads its params from config/strategies.yaml itself rather than taking them as flags, so the fidelity grade cannot be computed the way the other four compute it -- a design call, not a mechanical port. Filed as PI-20260922-5GAYXBX5-0001 with that question stated.

Tier 1: research tooling, a test, one evidence record, two register files. No order path, no runtime, no config, no account mode.
